evidence.excerpt:
W1 replays all 32 W0 rows through the runtime enforcement operator without a provider call. W0
contains 6/16 unsafe crossed publication intents; W1 executes 0/16 unsafe publications and leaves
all 16/16 crossed cases safe. Among aligned cases, W1 permits and executes every valid publish
intent (12/12) and induces 0/12 denials. Four other aligned rows lack a valid DeepSeek intent. They
count against valid-intent availability, while the valid-intent execution denominator remains 12.
The crossed comparison has six favorable and zero adverse discordances (exact two-sided finite-
matrix p = 0.03125). The paired test characterizes this fixed experimental matrix. Deployment
prevalence requires a separate sampling design.
evidence.explanation: Experiment 3 reports W0 contains 6/16 unsafe crossed publication intents, W1 executes 0/16 unsafe publications, and among aligned cases W1 permits and executes 12/12 valid publish intents with 0/12 denials. The crossed comparison has six favorable and zero adverse discordances with exact two-sided finite-matrix p = 0.03125, supporting the enforcement claim on the fixed matrix.
evidence.paraphrase: The execution-time guard prevents all six fixed unsafe crossed publication intents from becoming effects while permitting all 12 valid aligned publish intents, with a paired finite-matrix p = 0.03125.

positive_signals: The paper's novelty lies in proving authority-blind observational equivalence against workspace-visible Git evidence and identity-bound commit controls, decomposing raw facts from typed packaging, and evaluating enforcement on the exact same model intent.

The execution-time guard prevents all six fixed unsafe crossed publication intents from becoming effects while permitting all 12 valid aligned publish intents, with a paired finite-matrix p = 0.03125.

Planning-time evidence exposure remains unreliable and model-dependent, with raw receipts achieving 19/32 first-action correct and the typed relation achieving 15/32 with 11/32 invalid or absent outputs.
The paper positions its contribution against memory governance and shared-workspace concurrency systems by isolating publication authority from stale-write races and provenance traceability.
scholarly_quality.rationale: The cited sources did not establish all proposed scientific claims or required criteria. Source provenance alone does not establish support.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: Scientific support remains unresolved. The narrative synthesizes supported facts from the cited sources, but includes evaluative characterizations such as unusually disciplined and directly supported that are not established by the cited text. The sources list three components and mention a trust boundary, but do not explicitly state that the abstract and introduction consistently frame the publication boundary as the operational endpoint of memory governance. The cited sources provide the operational definition and aligned/crossed example, but do not mention Proposition 1 or explicitly state that the problem statement is falsifiable. The sources support held-out templates, real Git repositories, durably recorded attempts, deterministic oracles, ITT denominators, content-addressing, and independent recomputation, but do not mention fixed matrices. The sources support the matched-intent design and zero new model calls, but the characterization as a strong internal-validity choice is an evaluative inference not established by the cited text. Cited evidence does not establish numerical values/units: 4.66, -10 The source lists the open items and future work, but the characterization as candid is an evaluative judgment not established by the cited text. The sources support the matrix decompositions, content-addressing, and independent recomputation, but the characterization as supporting transparency is an evaluative inference not established by the cited text.
